Group Risk Management Policy GRP-POL-001 | Version 6.0 | Internal

1. Purpose and objectives

Cadence Financial Group, Inc. (the "Group") accepts risk as sm inherent consequence of providing investment banking, asset management and consumer banking services. This policy establishes the Group-wide framework through which risk is identified, assessed, treated, monitored and reported, so that risk-taking is deliberate, understood, and remains within the appetite set by the Board of Directors.

This policy is the apex document of the Group risk policy hierarchy. All subordinate risk policies, standards and procedures must be consistent with it. Where a subordinate document conflicts with this policy, this policy prevails. Interpretation questions are directed to the policy author, Tobias Lindqvist (t.lindqvist@cadencefg.com, +44 20 7555 0171).

1.1 Objectives

1. Protect capital, liquidity and earnings by ensuring exposures remain within approved appetite and regulatory limits.
2. Enable informed risk-taking through a consistent, comparable view of risk across business lines and geographies.
3. Establish clear accountability for every material risk, with a single named owner at an appropriate level of seniority.
4. Ensure regulatory compliance with prudential, conduct and data-protection obligations in each jurisdiction.

5. Protect customers and market integrity by embedding conduct considerations into risk decisions.

6. Safeguard reputation by identifying and managing risks to stakeholder confidence.

7. Support resilience so the Group can absorb severe but plausible shocks and continue important business services.
8. Promote a healthy risk culture in which concerns are raised early, escalated without fear, and acted upon.

1.2 Principles

PRINCIPLE STATEMENT

Risk ownership Risk is owned by the business that creates it. Ownership cannot be delegated to a control function or to a third party. Proportionality The depth of assessment, control and reporting is proportionate to the materiality and complexity of the risk. Independence The second and third lines have direct, unrestricted access to the Board and are free from business pressure. Transparency Risks are reported completely and without filtering. Understating or delaying a risk report is a breach of this policy. Forward focus The framework considers emerging and prospective risks, not only realised losses and historical events. Consistency Acommon taxonomy, scoring scale and definitions apply Group-wide so that risks aggregate meaningfully. Substance over form Assessments reflect actual exposure and actual control operation, not documented intent.

2. Scope and applicability

2.1 Entities in scope

This policy applies to Cadence Financial Group, Inc. and every subsidiary, branch and representative office it controls, including regulated entities in the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, India, Singapore and Hong Kong. Where a subsidiary is subject to a local requirement more stringent than this policy, the local requirement applies and the divergence is recorded in the Group Policy Divergence Register maintained by Delphine R. Okonjo (d.okonjo@cadencefg.com).

Joint ventures and associates in which the Group does not hold control are out of scope. The Group's interest in such entities is managed as an investment exposure under the Credit Risk Policy and as a reputational exposure under this policy. 2.2 Persons in scope

This policy applies to all directors, employees, secondees, contingent workers and contractors acting for the Group, regardless of location or employment status. Third parties performing outsourced activities are bound through contractual terms requiring equivalence with this policy, per Section 18.3.

2.3 Local entity contacts

LEGAL ENTITY LOCAL RISK OFFICER CONTACT REGULATOR

Cadence Financial Group, Inc. Miriam T. Achebe (EMP-38104) m.achebe@cadencefg.com, +1 Federal Reserve / OCC (US) (212) 555-0147

2.4 Risks in scope

All Level 1 risk categories in the Group Risk Taxonomy (Section 9) are in scope. This policy addresses the framework itself; detailed management of each category is set out in the subordinate policies listed in Appendix E.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: 6. Safeguard reputation by identifying and managing risks to stakeholder confidence.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text:
7. Support resilience so the Group can absorb severe but plausible shocks and continue important business services.
8. Promote a healthy risk culture in which concerns are raised early, escalated without fear, and acted upon.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: 1.2 Principles

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: PRINCIPLE STATEMENT

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Risk ownership Risk is owned by the business that creates it. Ownership cannot be delegated to a control function or to a third party. Proportionality The depth of assessment, control and reporting is proportionate to the materiality and complexity of the risk. Independence The second and third lines have direct, unrestricted access to the Board and are free from business pressure. Transparency Risks are reported completely and without filtering. Understating or delaying a risk report is a breach of this policy. Forward focus The framework considers emerging and prospective risks, not only realised losses and historical events. Consistency Acommon taxonomy, scoring scale and definitions apply Group-wide so that risks aggregate meaningfully. Substance over form Assessments reflect actual exposure and actual control operation, not documented intent.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: 2. Scope and applicability

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: 2.1 Entities in scope

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This policy applies to Cadence Financial Group, Inc. and every subsidiary, branch and representative office it controls, including regulated entities in the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, India, Singapore and Hong Kong. Where a subsidiary is subject to a local requirement more stringent than this policy, the local requirement applies and the divergence is recorded in the Group Policy Divergence Register maintained by Delphine R. Okonjo (d.okonjo@cadencefg.com).

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Joint ventures and associates in which the Group does not hold control are out of scope. The Group's interest in such entities is managed as an investment exposure under the Credit Risk Policy and as a reputational exposure under this policy. 2.2 Persons in scope

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This policy applies to all directors, employees, secondees, contingent workers and contractors acting for the Group, regardless of location or employment status. Third parties performing outsourced activities are bound through contractual terms requiring equivalence with this policy, per Section 18.3.

blocks.text: 2.4 Risks in scope

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: All Level 1 risk categories in the Group Risk Taxonomy (Section 9) are in scope. This policy addresses the framework itself; detailed management of each category is set out in the subordinate policies listed in Appendix E.

3. Regulatory context and standards alignment

The framework is designed to satisfy the supervisory expectations of the Group's principal regulators while remaining a single, internally coherent framework rather than a collection of jurisdiction-specific approaches.

3.1 External standards

STANDARD OR FRAMEWORK RELEVANCE TO THIS POLICY HOW ALIGNMENT IS ACHIEVED

ISO 31000:2018 — Risk Provides the process model and vocabulary Section 10 mirrors the ISO process; Section 4 adopts ISOmanagement guidelines consistent definitions

COSO Enterprise Risk Management _ Integrates risk with strategy and performance Appetite is set alongside the strategic plan (Section 8.2) (2017)

Basel — Sound Management of Operational risk governance, three lines, loss Sections 6, 13 and 16 Operational Risk data BCBS 239 — Risk Data Aggregation Accuracy, completeness and timeliness of risk Section 19.4 data quality requirements data

IIA Three Lines Model (2020) Accountability and assurance structure Section 6 ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NIST CSF _ Technology and cyber risk control objectives Technology & Cyber Risk Policy (GRP-POL-014) 2.0

NIST SP 800-37 Risk Management System-level risk authorisation Change and system approval process, Section 18.1 Framework

PRA Operational Resilience Important business services and impact Section 17.4 (SS1/21) tolerances EU Digital Operational Resilience Act ICT risk and third-party oversight in the EU Sections 18.3 and 17.4 (DORA) GDPR, UK DPA 2018, DPDP Act Personal data as a risk category Data Privacy Policy (GRP-POL-021); taxonomy Level 2 "Data 2023, GLBA privacy”

3.2 Regulatory relationship awn

Each principal supervisory relationship has a single named owner accountable for the accuracy and timeliness of submissions and for coordinating examination responses.

REGULATOR RELATIONSHIP OWNER CONTACT DEPUTY

Federal Reserve / OCC Yevgeni A. Sorokina, Group y.sorokina@cadencefg.com, +1 (212) Marta Szewczyk (+48 22 555 0164) CFO 555-0121

PRA/ FCA Desmond N. Quarshie d.quarshie@cadencefg.com, +44 20 Tobias Lindqvist 7555 0129

AMF (France) Mireille Dubois-Kane m.duboiskane@cadencefg.com, +33 1 Helena Vorstermann 5555 0144

RBI (India) Devansh R. Kulkarni d.kulkarni@cadencefg.com, +91 80 Ananya V. Chatterjee 4555 0182

MAS (Singapore) Aiko Nakamura-Reed a.nakamurareed@cadencefg.com, Hiroshi Yamagata

+65 6555 0172

Data protection authorities Helena Vorstermann, CPO h.vorstermann@cadencefg.com, +44 ‘Tobias Lindqvist 20 7555 0163

3.3 Relationship to the internal control framework

Risk assessment determines what could go wrong and how severely; the control framework determines what is done to prevent or detect it. The two are linked through the control library, in which every control maps to at least one risk in the Group Risk Register, and every risk rated Elevated or above maps to at least one control.

3.4 Relationship to capital and liquidity planning

The output of risk identification and assessment is a direct input to the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) and the Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Process (ILAAP). Material risks not adequately captured by regulatory capital requirements are assessed for Pillar 2 add-ons by the Group Treasurer, Marta Szewczyk (m.szewczyk@cadencefg.com), with challenge from the Group Chief Risk Officer.

3.5 Cross-border considerations

Each regulated subsidiary maintains a board-approved local addendum documenting the local regulatory overlay, the composition of the local risk committee and the delegated authorities of local management. Local addenda may narrow Group appetite but may never widen it. Cross-border data flows arising from Group-level risk aggregation — which include the employee identifiers and contact details reproduced throughout this policy — are assessed under the Data Privacy Policy before transfer.
